Button draft

Action trigger: accent-filled primary with corner brackets, outlined secondary. Renders a native <a> when href is set (all measured site usages navigate), a native <button> otherwise.

Variants: primary secondary · A11y: pending

Hover and focus-visible are CSS states, never props (RFC §3). Chrome lives in button.css; the type/button text-style values are restated there until a text-style extraction stage exists.

RFC: Button.rfc.md · Figma node: 16:18

States

Hover and focus-visible are CSS states, never props (RFC §3). Each stage below shows the examples held in that exact state via docs-only mirror rules derived from the component's own stylesheet.

default

The resting chrome — what every example renders.

Open the guide

hover

Versus default: primary's fill lightens toward white and an accent glow ring appears; secondary recolors its border and label to the accent. Pure CSS, never a prop (RFC §3).

Open the guide

focus-visible

Versus default: a 2px accent outline at 3px offset, both variants. Keyboard-only — pointer clicks never show it (RFC §4.2).

Open the guide

Props

PropTypeDefaultOptionalNote
variant "primary" | "secondary" primary no
href string — yes renders a native <a> with identical chrome; type is then ignored
type "button" | "submit" | "reset" button no button rendering only
onClick (e: MouseEvent) => void — yes

Accessibility pending

Semantic structure
Native <button type> or native <a href> when href is set; link semantics kept deliberately (Enter activates, Space scrolls). No ARIA overrides; uppercase is CSS text-transform, AT reads the author's casing.
Keyboard
Native activation, no custom key handling; focus ring only on :focus-visible — 2px accent outline, 3px offset, both variants.
Decisions
Corner brackets and hover glow are decorative pseudo-elements/box-shadow, invisible to AT. Disabled is out of v1 by arbitration (RFC §7). Contrast is computed by the gate from resolved tokens, never declared here.
Notes
Implemented per RFC §4; this status moves to pass only through the accessibility engine gate, never by assertion.
